title: Enhancing End of Life with Choices and Dignity
what_it_is: Enhancing End of Life with Choices and Dignity

sections.label: Dying at home survey
sections.summary: A 2014 Lien Foundation survey found 77% of Singaporeans wanted to die at home, but as of 2017 only about 30% did.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A 2014 survey by the Lien Foundation found that 77% of Singaporeans wanted to die at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, as of 2017, only about 30% did so, with the other 70% dying in hospitals, nursing homes, hospices and other settings.

sections.label: AMD, LPA, ACP adoption
sections.summary: As of 2015 about 24,682 Singaporeans registered for AMD, 43,000 submitted LPA by March 2018, and 4,500 ACPs were completed in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nationally, the adoption levels of these instruments reflect responses of the small group I surveyed – with only about 24,682 Singaporeans having registered for AMD as of 2015, 43,000 having submitted their LPA as of March 2018, although the numbers are growing and only 4,500 instances of ACP were completed in 2018.

sections.label: ACP uptake and palliative need
sections.summary: A 2019 ACP database study showed 1.44% of chronically ill patients took up ACP, while WHO estimates 56.8 million people yearly need palliative care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A study of the ACP database in 2019 showed that only 1.44% of chronically ill patients took up ACP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: WHO estimates that each year, about 56.8 million people, including 25.7 million in their last year of life, need palliative care.

sections.label: IAMGoingHome ICU transfer pilot
sections.summary: The writer applauds Ng Teng Fong General Hospital's IAMGoingHome pilot, started last October, which transfers patients who desire to die at home from ICU.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I read with comfort The Straits Times article published recently on 1 May, titled "Leaving ICU to die at home, surrounded by family and familiar comforts".

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I applaud the medical teams at Ng Teng Fong General Hospital for piloting "IAMGoingHome" since October last year, smoothening the workflows from both the intensive care unit (ICU) and Supportive Care and Palliative Medicine at the hospital to safely transfer patients, who no longer seek aggressive treatments and desire to die at home, to reach home smoothly for their last wish to be fulfilled.

sections.label: Hospice day care and respite
sections.summary: The writer asks how many hospice day care centres exist and whether the Government would provide or expand respite care services for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry clarify how many hospice day care centres for the terminally ill are there?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider providing respite care services for the caregiver, or make it more available like in Australia, where dying at home is more common?

sections.label: MediSave claims by palliative professionals
sections.summary: Currently only healthcare professionals specialising in palliative care can assist patients in making MediSave claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, only healthcare professionals who specialise in palliative care can assist patients in making MediSave claims.

sections.label: TTSH Dover Park Hospice pilot
sections.summary: The speaker asks about the TTSH-Dover Park Hospice pilot for seamless care and suggests subsidies for professional palliative caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Additionally, I am interested in the progress of the pilot programme between Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH) and Dover Park Hospice, which aims to provide patients with timely and seamless care across different settings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we also consider providing subsidies for professional palliative caregiving?

sections.label: Capitation funding and palliative affordability
sections.summary: The speaker asks how shifting to a capitation funding model will help the affordability of palliative care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In addition, how will the shift to a capitation funding model for our healthcare help in the affordability of palliative care?

sections.label: Dying at home wishes
sections.summary: The speaker says most Singaporeans want to die at home and wants a quick, peaceful death with support for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Reports have consistent findings that the majority of Singaporeans would like to die at home surrounded by loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: But, like Ling Ling and many others, I do want to die at home surrounded by loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: But I also want a quick and peaceful death, without being sustained artificially by tubes and machines, and with no regrets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: To live a life worth living is to be prepared to die at any time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: And if I do not go as quickly, I would want those who care for me to be supported emotionally and financially in my final days.

sections.label: Palliative care subsidies
sections.summary: The Government provides subsidies of up to 80% for palliative care and home-based respite care for caregivers of end-of-life patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To keep palliative care affordable, the Government provides subsidies of up to 80% for palliative care, as well as home-based respite care services for caregivers of end-of-life patients.

sections.label: Bundled funding pilot
sections.summary: The Dover Park Hospice and TTSH pilot will trial bundled funding for palliative care across three community settings, such as per-patient per month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Instead of capitation funding, the pilot between Dover Park Hospice and TTSH will trial bundled funding for palliative care services across all three community settings, for example, on a per-patient per month basis.

sections.label: Pilot launch second half
sections.summary: Work with Dover Park Hospice and TTSH refined the pilot design and evaluation, aiming to launch in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have been working closely with Dover Park Hospice and TTSH to refine the pilot design and develop a robust evaluation and monitoring process to track effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We aim to launch the pilot in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Enhanced financial support schemes
sections.summary: Financial support schemes like the Home Caregiving Grant and Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund were enhanced to support informal caregiving costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have enhanced financial support schemes, like the Home Caregiving Grant and the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund, to better support costs of informal caregiving.

sections.label: Payouts for severe disability
sections.summary: Singaporeans with severe disability can currently receive payouts of up to about $1,300 a month through these schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Through these schemes, Singaporeans with severe disability can currently benefit from payouts of up to about $1,300 a month.

sections.label: Pre-planning awareness campaign
sections.summary: MOH, MSF and PSD are planning a three-year campaign to increase awareness and adoption of pre-planning instruments, focusing on LPA and ACP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MOH, MSF and PSD are also planning a three-year campaign to increase awareness and adoption of pre-planning instruments with a focus on LPA and ACP.

sections.label: Palliative care strategy and adjournment
sections.summary: Partners were gathered to refresh the national palliative care strategy, and the House was adjourned, with the next Sitting at 12.00 noon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This is not change that will happen overnight, but I am confident that it is one which will gather pace in the coming years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have gathered key partners to refresh our national strategy for palliative care and will share more in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But to ensure that Singaporeans live well and leave well, all of us have to play our roles as family members, caregivers and friends and have conversations about what a good death looks like.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I adjourn the House pursuant to the Standing Order.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 12.00 noon.
